newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CSOB SAYS DEBT TALKS WITH SLOVAKIA INTENSIFY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CSOB SAYS DEBT TALKS WITH SLOVAKIA INTENSIFY.

text.p: Czech bank CSOB on Thursday said talks over debts owed to it by Slovakia dating back to the split of former federation partner Czechoslovakia have intensified, though no agreement has been reached.
Before the country split in 1993, CSOB, the former Czechoslovak foreign trade bank, loaned both Czech and Slovak firms some 30.5 billion crowns to finance exports to other communist countries.
Now it is looking for both countries to repay the loans under a formula struck during the split whereby Slovakia assumed one-third of Czechoslovakia's debt, and the Czech Republic two-thirds.
"We are now holding negotiations with the Slovak National Bank (NBS) and the Finance Ministry about CSOB receivables in the Slovak Collection Unit (SCU)," CSOB spokesman Milan Tomanek told Reuters.
"(They) are the most intensive since since we started." He did not say how close to an agreement the two sides were.
The SCU was formed to take on the Slovak part of the debts, but Slovak officials have reportedly been reluctant to payoff the debt, which has now grown to some 13 billion crowns.
The Czech Collection Unit, which took two-thirds of the Czecholsovak debt, has been paying its debt to CSOB on schedule.
However, Tomanek said: "We have all the reasons to believe the SCU will pay its debt to CSOB." He declined to comment on the reasons for the delay in ending the talks.
Some banking sources have said CSOB has quitely tried to pressure Slovak officials into at least giving a guarantee it would redeem the debt, though Tomanek would not comment on the issue.
